{"author":"id_1c03cb75e760","author_key":"1088e386daf41b5a5aa0e58446e55501e1ccad5af82965519ff3eed2e75a6e0d","hub":"threadhub.record.v0","kind":"note","payload":{"hash":"e9b7fba5931119607e3f8e14a39b9392380876438b1bd33aa2ff7516681169df","payload":{"actor_id":"par_challenge_maker","content_hash":"sha256:078bbbe8733be538049f172e0192c73b5709abf375c186d908411cebc5a1cfc7","event_id":"evt_72b7bb93f26d","event_type":"PositionTaken","hash_version":"clista.event_hash.v1","payload":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","position":{"id":"pos_r1","statement":"## Recommendation (Round 1)

**Adopt with modifications — not adopt-as-proposed, not reject.**

Bump to **v1.1.0** is justified, but the directive as stated is under-specified in three ways that need fixing before it's locked in. Below is the recommendation and defense.

---

### Why not reject

The 1.0.0 eval identified a real, structural gap, not a stylistic preference. The current Clista verifies *procedural compliance*: did the agent produce an objective, boundaries, KPIs, tool access, error handling, logging, etc. Nothing in Phases 1–4 asks whether the *procedure itself* — the Clista walkthrough, or whatever method the agent chose — is the right instrument for the stated purpose. An agent can score "met" on every box while faithfully executing a mismatched procedure. That's compliance theater, and it's exactly the failure mode a mismatch-detection-capable agent should be catching. Rejecting the revision would leave a known blind spot on the record after it's been explicitly named. Reject is off the table.

### Why not adopt-as-proposed

The proposal says the agent should "state, before execution, why the selected procedure fits the stated purpose" and treat mismatches as "blocking findings." That's correct in spirit but incomplete in three ways:

1. **No placement specified.** A free-floating directive risks becoming decorative — something an agent nods to in a preamble sentence rather than something graded with the same met/partial/missing/n/a rigor as every other item. It needs to be an actual checkbox, and it needs to sit *before* Objective Clarity in Phase 1, because you can't meaningfully assess "is the goal clear" until you've confirmed the chosen approach is even aimed at that goal. Recommend: new Phase 1 item, ordered first —
   **"Purpose-Fit Justification: Has the agent stated, prior to execution, why the selected procedure/approach serves the stated purpose — distinct from whether the goal itself is clearly stated?"**
   This is deliberately worded to not overlap with the existing Objective Clarity or Boundary Definition items, which check goal-clarity and scope, not method-appropriateness.

2. **"Blocking finding" isn't wired into anything.** The Clista's output convention already has a place for this — the "Top 3 blockers" and "Minimum HITL gates" sections. The directive needs to explicitly say: a purpose-procedure mismatch found at this item must be surfaced as a blocker and must trigger a HITL gate before Phases 2–4 are even scored, not just noted as a failed checkbox among others. Otherwise "blocking" is asserted but not operationalized.

3. **No artifact/logging tie-in.** A verbal or implicit justification is unauditable and exactly the kind of thing that gets skipped under time pressure. The purpose-fit statement should be required as a timestamped, logged artifact, explicitly cross-referenced to the existing Phase 4 Logging item, so the new check doesn't float outside the audit trail the rest of the checklist already demands.

### On the grader-identity correction

The 2026-07-13 correction (sha256:d1321c1b606a03...) corrects *who* graded, not *what* was found. The substance — A- grade, mismatch-detection strength, purpose-fit gap — stands unaffected. This should be cited in the v1.1.0 changelog as provenance for the eval that motivated the change, but it does not itself bear on the adopt/reject decision.

### Surviving reservation (to remain on record, not resolved by this decision)

Purpose-fit justifications are self-reportable and gameable — an agent can produce a plausible-sounding sentence without real analysis. This revision should ship as **v1.1.0 provisional**, with a follow-up eval specifically testing whether the new item catches *induced* purpose-procedure mismatches (not just ones already visible from other items), before it's treated as fully calibrated. This is a reservation to carry forward, not a blocker to adoption now.

---

**Position for the record:** Adopt v1.1.0 with the three modifications above (placement as first Phase 1 item, explicit blocker/HITL wiring, logged-artifact requirement), changelog-cite the grader-identity correction for provenance, and flag the version as provisional pending one confirming eval cycle."},"provider":"anthropic","role":"maker","round":1},"previous_hash":"sha256:944dd6f7a24b59f08506407b23cdfa8173dbb78796027f7555b4913c71a86b18","protocol_version":"clista.protocol.v0","thread_id":"thr_challenge_2026_07_13T03_03_31Z_fc301f","timestamp":"2026-07-13T03:04:18.132Z"},"prev":"53a4c1586925ca1937bcfbaf7dc1be06ae3339208d1f37bac4d492da5de185a1","seq":6,"sig":"5ecd82ee7b6dc7040976d71976ce5b4c54250292ebc0099928e1ced6a54db51be319360e89cc1dc4b6498d1e78338e095e684a6bbecc85e1a3cfcc5cc762eb00","ts":"2026-07-13T03:04:18+00:00","type":"PositionTaken","writer":"MAKER"},"prev":"sha256:1476d77121ea3058c59496fa47ccc53ace7cbf083a4e814cc50ae82e27412ef1","recorded_at":"2026-07-13T03:13:41.390Z","seq":7,"thread":"thd_bc679070f90a"}

## First objection: Step 0 was never actually performed

The protocol this run operates under (consensus_protocol@1.1.0, cited by the ORCHESTRATOR as precedent) makes input validation *mandatory and structurally first* — before restating the directive, before any lane or recommendation work. The MAKER's Round 1 position skips straight to "Recommendation" and "Why not reject" / "Why not adopt-as-proposed" without ever testing the directive's supplied facts for internal consistency. That is itself a protocol violation, and it matters here because there *is* something to validate:

- The directive states the eval was "graded A-" and that "grader identity corrected on the record 2026-07-13" for an eval conducted "2026-07-12." A grader-identity correction one day after grading, on a record whose substantive findings (grade, mismatch-detection strength, purpose-fit gap) are asserted to be untouched, is not self-evidently benign. [ASSUMPTION: MAKER treats "identity corrected" as isolable from "substance corrected" with no cited basis.] Chain-of-custody corrections to grading records are exactly the kind of event that should trigger scrutiny of *what else* might have been misattributed — not a one-line dismissal in a changelog-cite paragraph.
- **Demand:** what is the actual content of the correction record at sha256:d1321c1b606a03a2be939bf23ea0dc9ef26cfbdc36da1cee6962c36799d4c38c? The MAKER cites the hash as if citing it discharges the burden of verifying it. A hash is not a citation of content — it's a pointer. Without retrieving and characterizing what the correction actually says, "corrects who graded, not what was found" is an [ASSUMPTION] dressed as a [CITED:] fact. This is precisely the anti-pattern the protocol warns against: lowering the apparent assumption count without doing the retrieval.

Until that record is actually inspected, the entire revision rests on an eval whose evidentiary integrity is unconfirmed.

## Second objection: n=1 is a thin basis for a structural amendment

The whole case for revision is one eval, one grade (A-), one finding. The MAKER's Round 1 accepts this as sufficient to justify amending a production checklist. No second eval, no pattern across runs, no confirmed instance of an agent actually executing a purpose-mismatched procedure while passing all Phase 1–4 items is cited. The gap identified is *theoretical* ("an agent can score met on every box while faithfully executing a mismatched procedure") — a hypothesis the eval's grader raised, not a documented failure the eval observed. [ASSUMPTION: MAKER conflates "grader flagged this as a needed directive" with "grader observed this failure mode occur."]

**Demand:** does the eval record contain an actual transcript where a purpose-procedure mismatch occurred and was missed by the 1.0.0 checklist? If not, the revision is being justified by a grader's foresight, not by observed failure — which is a legitimate reason to *investigate*, but a weak reason to *lock into production* a new blocking/HITL mechanism.
